Of course, I need to change it.' No clinician, medication or clearance is mentioned at any point.

signals: Proposed label: the_negotiator — a commercially experienced buyer with no affordability constraint who treats the price as a term to be negotiated and will transact only if he extracts a concession. He says so explicitly: 'I have everything decided ... I have a gut feeling, it's pricey, if you can come down with a price, let's get on, if you cannot, it's fine, I will find out in another way.'
Not an affordability objection — he never claims he cannot pay, only that the price must be 'fair enough for me'

Nearest existing avatar is the_rebuilder: near 40, disc problem, high blood pressure, morning stiffness, 'I feel like I'm going in a slope downwards, from now on, and I just want to compensate this one with serious changes'

Does not fit skeptical_bargain_hunter — his alternative is not cheap and he has not tried it: 'I don't train with none of them. So I don't know which one is doing what, but it's not cheap, to be honest.'
Does not fit the_optimizer — price is unambiguously a barrier and a negotiating lever rather than a quality signal

objections.raw_quote: You are pricey. ... It's, you know, I can get the same, for the same money, training with the guy, two times per week, and the rest they have to do it alone, of course, in his own team, because they have some, and it's quite, not so far away from my office.
objections.rep_response: Reframed against the personal-trainer business model — 'Trevor is operating a different business model. Like, our idea is not to have you for life' — which the prospect answered by pointing out the local coaches he researched use the same transformation positioning.

objections.raw_quote: So I would like to know what is your best price for me. Because, you know, if I have to decide it now, then I need to know the best price. And I will tell you. Honestly, it's yes or no.
objections.rep_response: Pulled back to goals first, then said 'I have no power over this price', then offered a three-month tier at $4,000, and finally agreed to take the prospect's own counteroffer to Trevor and the team. Proposed label: discount_demand.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I know. But for 4K, in three months, it's like I'm paying more than for the six months. I know you're short in the period, but the price is high. I for me, I think I need guidance, I think, on the six months
objections.rep_response: Argued he should start with three months, see results, and pay the remaining $2,000 to complete the six months. The prospect did not accept and returned to the discount request.

objections.raw_quote: I don't get so much in detail with them as I did with you, but they follow the same principle. You have to have a significant lifestyle change, physique. So of course, health overall, I talk with them. So I don't know where to put Trevor.

outcome.next_step: Rep to consult Trevor and the team on the $5,000 counteroffer and revert within one to three days

notable.note: A sixteen-minute price negotiation in which the prospect ran the process. The rep said 'I have no power over this price', then offered an unlisted $4,000 three-month tier, then agreed to take a $5,000-for-six-months counteroffer to Trevor — three positions in eleven minutes. The prospect had already priced the reduced tier correctly as worse value per month. Separately and more seriously, this is a prospect with a spinal disc problem and self-attributed high blood pressure, both named on the call by the rep, and both used to build urgency ('this is something that you cannot neglect') rather than to trigger any question about medical clearance for loaded kettlebell training. The rep also told him 'no one has ever bargained with me to drop the price', which is contradicted by his own calls earlier in this same batch.

quality.notes: Short file with frequent inversion, worst in the negotiation from 00:11:39 onward where the rep's and prospect's lines interleave under the wrong labels — 'Let me ask you this, like, whenever, like, when is the moment that we actually become sure of something?' is the rep's, and 'It's a good speech, Andrew' is the prospect's, both mis-assigned. The prospect's connection drops and freezes at least twice, and he says so, so some content is missing rather than merely mislabelled.
